Class ADRCController

java.lang.Object
yams.core.math.ADRCController
public class ADRCController extends Object
Active disturbance rejection controller.

Written by FRC Team 8331, who contributed active disturbance rejection control to YAMS.

An active disturbance rejection controller treats every unmodeled effect (friction, gravity, back-EMF, coupling, dropped battery voltage, external loads) as a single "total disturbance" and estimates it online with an extended state observer. The controller then cancels the estimate while driving the modeled part of the plant with a bandwidth-parameterized control law. Because the disturbance estimate absorbs plant mismatch, the controller needs very little model knowledge: just the system order and an approximate input gain b0.

Most teams do not construct this class directly; they describe the controller with ADRCConfig and the motor controller builds and runs it. This class is the engine underneath, useful for custom loops and for understanding what the configuration produces.

The controller supports plant orders 1 through 4: order 1 for velocity loops (a flywheel or shooter wheel), order 2 for position loops (an arm or elevator), and orders 3 and 4 for mechanisms whose measured output sits further integrations behind the input. The extended state observer is one order higher than the plant, with its final state holding the disturbance estimate. Gains are generated from a single closed-loop bandwidth wc; the observer bandwidth is 4 * wc.

The controller keeps only its running state: the observer's estimate, its last outputs and the tracking differentiator. Everything else it reads from its ADRCConfig, including the observer and control gains, which the config works out again whenever its settling time, bandwidth scale or b0 changes. So every live-tunable value takes effect on the next step. The system order, input delay and tracking differentiator are fixed when the controller is initialized.

The controller does not limit or ramp its output. A motor controller running it limits and ramps the output itself, with withClosedLoopControllerMaximumVoltage(...) and withClosedLoopRampRate(...), and tells the observer the voltage it applied. Run on its own, clamp the output to what the actuator can apply, ramp it with WPILib's SlewRateLimiter if it needs one, and tell the observer what was applied with calculate(double, double, double), so a clamped output is not mistaken for a disturbance.

Example velocity control

// A first-order velocity plant driven by volts, with b0 in (rotations per second) per volt
// per second.
ADRCController adrc = new ADRCController(new ADRCConfig()
    .withSystemOrder(SystemOrder.FIRST)
    .withSettlingTime(Seconds.of(0.2)));
// b0, which the config leaves unset, and the control period.
adrc.initialize(b0, Milliseconds.of(20));

// In periodic(): clamp the output, and tell the observer what was applied last loop.
double volts = MathUtil.clamp(adrc.calculate(
    flywheel.getSpeed().in(RotationsPerSecond), // measurement
    setpoint.in(RotationsPerSecond),            // reference
    motor.getAppliedVoltage()), -12, 12);       // applied last loop

Keep b0 in the units of the loop: for a velocity loop it is the velocity change per second per volt.

    • initialize

      public void initialize(double b0, org.wpilib.units.measure.Time period)
      Initialize the controller: give its config the values it cannot hold itself, which also works out its gains, and start the observer and the output at zero.
      Parameters:
      b0 - Input gain used while the config leaves b0 unset, such as the one ADRCConfig.resolveB0(DCMotor, SmartMotorControllerConfig) derives. Must be finite and non-zero when used.
      period - Control period. Must be finite and positive.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if a value is invalid, or the tracking differentiator cannot run at this period.

    • calculate

      public double calculate(double measurement, double setpoint, double appliedOutput)
      Run one control step, telling the observer what the actuator really applied last step.

      A motor controller does not always apply what it is asked for: a current limit, a low battery or its own saturation can apply less. The observer works out the disturbance from the output it believes moved the plant, so if it is told the output it asked for while the motor got less, it mistakes the shortfall for a disturbance, winds up, and can settle into a limit cycle. Giving it the applied output keeps its estimate true to what moved the mechanism.

      Parameters:
      measurement - Measured output.
      setpoint - Reference.
      appliedOutput - Output the actuator applied since the last step, such as the motor controller's measured voltage. A non-finite value is ignored.
      Returns:
      Controller output.
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the controller has not been initialized.

    • calculate

      public double calculate(double measurement, ADRCController.Reference now, ADRCController.Reference next, double appliedOutput)
      Run one control step on a moving setpoint, such as a motion profile's, telling the observer what the actuator really applied last step.

      The controller is given the setpoint where it is now, at the start of the control period, and where it will be at the end, as WPILib's feedforwards are. It follows the setpoint now, and feeds forward how it moves over the period: a first order loop the average rate over the period, and a higher order loop the rate now and the change of rate over the period. Given only the setpoint at the end of the period, its stiff feedback would pull the mechanism a period ahead of the profile. A setpoint standing still is Reference.still(setpoint) for both. A tracking differentiator, when the config turns one on, replaces the rates with its own.

      Parameters:
      measurement - Measured output.
      now - The setpoint now, and its rate.
      next - The setpoint one control period from now, and its rate.
      appliedOutput - Output the actuator applied since the last step, such as the motor controller's measured voltage. A non-finite value is ignored.
      Returns:
      Controller output.
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the controller has not been initialized.

    • reset

      public void reset(double measurement)
      Reset the observer state from a measured output.

      The measured state starts where the mechanism is, so enabling the controller does not look like a step from zero. The remaining states, including the disturbance estimate, start at zero, and the output history starts at zero because the motors were unpowered. The tracking differentiator, when enabled, also starts at the measurement.

      Parameters:
      measurement - Initial measured output, in the units the controller is stepped with.
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the controller has not been initialized.
      IllegalArgumentException - if measurement is not finite.

    • reset

      public void reset(double[] xhatInit, double uInit)
      Reset the observer state and output history.

      Both observers start from the supplied state. The tracking differentiator, when enabled, starts at xhatInit[0] (or zero when xhatInit is null).

      Parameters:
      xhatInit - Initial observer state, length systemOrder + 1. null starts at zero.
      uInit - Initial output.
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the controller has not been initialized.
      IllegalArgumentException - if xhatInit has the wrong length or uInit is not finite.

    • getEstimatedStates

      public double[] getEstimatedStates()
      Get the extended state observer's state estimate.

      Entry 0 is the estimated measured output, entries 1..systemOrder-1 are the remaining plant states, and the final entry is the total disturbance estimate.

      Returns:
      Copy of the observer state, length systemOrder + 1.
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the controller has not been initialized.

    • getEstimatedDisturbance

      public double getEstimatedDisturbance()
      Get the estimated total disturbance.

      This is the final observer state, in the units of the plant's highest derivative per second. Divide by b0 to view it as an equivalent control input.

      Returns:
      Estimated total disturbance.
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the controller has not been initialized.
